questions.stem: After anaesthesia, must a breastfeeding mother pump and discard milk for 24 hours?
options: No, sleep and keep is advised

questions.stem: Which analgesics are considered safe for a breastfeeding mother after surgery?
Do anaesthetic and analgesic drugs pass into breast milk?
options: Yes, in tiny, clinically insignificant amounts

questions.stem: How is the relative infant dose (RID) calculated for a breastfed infant?
questions.answer: Infant dose via milk (mg/kg/day) divided by maternal dose (mg/kg/day)

questions.stem: Which relative infant dose is considered safe for a breastfed infant?
Morphine has a relative infant dose of about what percentage, despite an excellent safety record?
Why is an opioid-sparing technique preferred for a breastfeeding mother?
questions.answer: Opioids and their metabolites pass into milk a little more

questions.stem: Which breast condition is a risk of stopping breastfeeding after surgery?
Which infant risk is linked to stopping breastfeeding after surgery?
What does stopping breastfeeding after surgery expose the infant to?
Which infants need caution with opioids while their mother breastfeeds?
questions.answer: Infants at high risk of apnoea, e.g. premature

questions.stem: Which infant condition means NSAIDs should be avoided in a breastfeeding mother?
Why should breastfeeding patients not avoid analgesia after surgery?
Which state should be avoided to support breastfeeding after surgery?
Where possible, which type of surgery suits a breastfeeding patient?
In preoperative assessment, which patients should be asked about breastfeeding?
options: Every patient with a child under 2 years
Only patients with a child under 6 months
Only patients with a child over 5 years

questions.stem: Which infant risk should be assessed before surgery in a breastfeeding mother?
Where on the operating list should a breastfeeding mother be placed, to shorten separation from her baby?
Why should fasting be kept short for a breastfeeding patient?
Which analgesic approach is preferred for a breastfeeding patient during surgery?
Above what daily oxycodone dose is more drowsiness seen in the baby of a breastfeeding mother?
After sugammadex, for how long should a woman on hormonal contraception use barrier methods?
When should a mother resume breastfeeding after anaesthesia?
options: As soon as alert and physically able
Only after drugs are cleared from milk

questions.stem: What postoperative strategy is advised for nausea and vomiting in breastfeeding patients?
questions.answer: Effective antiemetic strategy, including prophylaxis if needed
